hints: Look at the table and count how many different DNA triplets are listed for each amino acid in methionine - isoleucine - cysteine - tryptophan.
Because the genetic code is degenerate, any triplet for one position can combine with any triplet for the next position, so multiply the counts for the four positions together.
walkthrough:
**Count the triplet choices for each amino acid**

Look carefully at the table for our sequence. Methionine has only 1 triplet (TAC). Isoleucine has 3 triplets (TAA, TAG, TAT). Cysteine has 2 triplets (ACA, ACG). Tryptophan has only 1 triplet (ACC).

**Use the multiplication rule for combinations**

Each choice is independent, so we multiply the number of options at each position to get all possible DNA sequences.

Key calculation:
$$1 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$$

**Conclude the maximum number**

There are 6 different ways to build a DNA sequence that still gives methionine - isoleucine - cysteine - tryptophan. This is due to degeneracy of the genetic code.

options.A: Not correct. 1 would mean no degeneracy, but isoleucine and cysteine each have more than one triplet code.
options.B: Not correct. 4 misses some combinations, you must multiply 3 options for isoleucine by 2 options for cysteine, not add them.
options.C: Correct. 1 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 6 different DNA sequences can all code for this same peptide.
options.D: Not correct. 7 comes from adding 1 + 3 + 2 + 1, but independent choices at each position must be multiplied, not added.
